name: Market Socialism
summary: Market socialism combines social ownership of the means of production, usually through worker cooperatives or public enterprises, with competitive markets for goods and often for capital goods. Its models differ over who owns firms and who controls investment, but all reject both capitalist ownership and comprehensive central planning. Adherents claim it can keep the efficiency and incentive signals of markets while ending wage labour and curbing inequality.
scope: The mainstream of the family as it is discussed today: Mill's cooperative vision, the Lange-Taylor-Dickinson model, Yugoslav self-management, and the modern designs of Roemer (coupon socialism), Bardhan, Corneo and Schweickart (economic democracy), with Wolff's worker self-directed enterprises. Anarchist mutualism (Proudhon, Warren) is noted as an ancestor but is not the basis of the profile. Because the ideology is an economic model, most statements outside economics are low-confidence inferences from its democratic, egalitarian leanings.

keyFigures.name: John Stuart Mill
keyFigures.role: Argued in 1848 that worker-owned associations competing in markets would come to predominate.

keyFigures.name: Oskar Lange
keyFigures.role: Developed the 1930s model of socialism with a planning board simulating market prices.

keyFigures.name: David Schweickart
keyFigures.role: Author of the economic democracy model of worker-run firms and public investment.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue for the model, but social ownership aimed at fairness and public provision of basics leads most adherents to support guaranteed public health care; inferred from the egalitarian goals.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In worker-run firms workers take the residual, so a wage floor matters little to the model itself; adherents are split between wage floors for remaining hired labour and the view that the issue falls away.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Market socialists hold that markets allocate goods and capital well but reject that they do so better without social ownership and public control of investment, so the statement is split.

public-ownership.rationale: Models differ: Lange and Roemer keep state or public enterprises, while Schweickart and Mill favour worker-run firms renting public capital, so adherents split on classic public utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Roemer, Bardhan and Corneo design systems to spread capital income and fund a social dividend, and Mill favoured limits on inheritance, so higher taxation of wealth fits the egalitarian aim.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the cooperative-labour tradition that backs worker power, though in worker-run firms the union role is less central than under capitalism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of productive property is removed or limited in every model, so private property cannot be a near-inviolable right, although personal property and savings remain.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Schweickart's model restricts firm growth and capital markets and favours price controls where needed; support for tighter regulation of any remaining corporations is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Schweickart's public sector acts as employer of last resort and the schemes aim at equal shares and a social dividend, so welfare cuts contradict the egalitarian design.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker cooperatives are the usual form in the models. Schweickart's workers control but rent capital from society and Mill expected collective ownership by workers, though state-owned variants exist, so agree not strongly.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by the model; as a democratic, liberal-leaning left tradition adherents are inferred to be wary of state surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The ideology is an economic model with no stated drug policy and adherents likely vary.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No stated position; liberal Millian roots and egalitarian concern pull in opposite directions.

strong-leader.rationale: Models stress democratic control at the firm and public level and critique authoritarian planning, so a leader bypassing gridlock is opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents inferred to be split.

state-harmful.rationale: The models need a state for public investment, the capital charge and price setting (Lange's planning board), so calling it unnecessary and harmful is rejected; Proudhonian mutualists are the exception.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; lower priority than social spending is inferred from the egalitarian left orientation.

decide-locally.rationale: Schweickart splits investment funds by region and community and favours firm-level democracy, but national investment and tax remain central.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No stated position; adherents inferred to be split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian, left-liberal orientation of most adherents.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that a progressive-left tradition does not treat traditional family structures as foundational.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the progressive-left milieu of contemporary market socialists.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the progressive-left milieu of contemporary adherents.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular left-liberal outlook.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the egalitarian commitments of contemporary adherents.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Outside the economic model; adherents likely split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Outside the economic model; no stated position.

gradual-change.rationale: Schweickart foresees elected leftist governments making a few reforms, but the end goal is a wholly new system, so neither gradualism nor rupture fits cleanly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the internationalist egalitarian orientation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Schweickart's model favours fair trade and domestic reinvestment of capital, which cuts against deeper integration; otherwise no stated position.

free-trade.rationale: Schweickart's model aims at fair rather than free trade with little cross-border capital flow, and public control of investment sits uneasily with unrestricted trade.

nation-first.rationale: The model keeps capital at home but takes no stand on putting national interest above global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents inferred to be split.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; adherents inferred to be split.

limit-growth.rationale: Schweickart argues that democratic firms lack a built-in drive to expand, but the models do not call for limiting growth; adherents vary.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Schweickart lists environmental damage among capitalism's structural flaws; inferred support for strong public action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; adherents inferred to be split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Models are designed to be introduced by democratic reform, elected governments and transition (Schweickart, Roemer, Mill's gradual associations), so revolution is not endorsed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lange's planning board relies on technicians but political control and workplace democracy are emphasized; inferred mild disagreement.

central-planning.rationale: Market socialism is defined against central planning, which Schweickart argues leads to authoritarianism and inefficiency.

socialized-markets.rationale: This is the defining claim: markets are retained, with social, worker or public ownership of firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Mill favoured taxing unearned land rent but replacing most other taxes with it is not a market-socialist position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Mill proposed limits on bequests and gifts to spread property; Roemer and Corneo similarly seek to prevent concentration of capital through inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Corneo and Roemer designs distribute a social dividend from public ownership of capital to citizens, which functions as a basic income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The model favours fair trade and domestic capital but no tariff policy is specified.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Social control of investment is central in Schweickart's public banks and Lange's planning board, though through democratic and market procedures rather than strategic-industry targeting.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Roemer and Bardhan spread shares equally across citizens, but productive property is socially held rather than owned by small owners, so the claim half fits.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Market socialism retains money, prices and markets, and in Roemer's coupon model citizens even use coupons for shares; wage labour is replaced by profit-sharing, but money remains.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Public banks are central to Schweickart's model, so leaving money to the market is rejected; inferred for the other models.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized employer and worker bodies setting wages and prices together is not part of the models; prices come from markets.

one-party-rule.rationale: Market socialists present these as democratic systems, in contrast with one-party planning.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the democratic and egalitarian orientation.

democracy-best.rationale: Democratic control of firms and investment is central, so democracy is valued; strong agreement on the clause about voters choosing badly is not documented.

direct-votes.rationale: Workplace and public votes are central, but direct legislation by citizens is not part of the models.

workers-councils.rationale: Workplace self-management is core (Yugoslavia), but councils as the basis of political power is a council-communist idea not endorsed by market socialists.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mill and market socialists reject inherited or natural privilege; the egalitarian one-person-one-vote model of firms rules this out.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; reform-oriented adherents lean to peaceful methods but justification of violence is not settled.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian democratic orientation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular liberal-left orientation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular democratic orientation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed directly; the models rely on public institutions, and Schweickart emphasises social over private control.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian left orientation.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian universalist orientation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Market socialists often reject the Marxist theory of history; Schweickart sidesteps Marx's deeper concepts, though some such as Wolff come from Marxism, so adherents are split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Roemer and Bardhan aim at equal access to capital income and Schweickart at reduced inequality, but market-set pay differences remain, so full equality of outcomes is not the aim.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the democratic orientation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mill defends competition but also cooperation; the models use self-interest through markets without treating it as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal democratic roots of Mill and modern adherents.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental concern appears but no stated stance on intrinsic value.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The models seek to reorganize industrial economies, not reject them.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Lange's trial-and-error and Dickinson's mathematical planning use calculation, but handing government decisions to algorithms is not stated.

restore-past-order.rationale: The models aim to build a new economic order, not restore an old one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Market socialism is often justified pragmatically on efficiency and feasibility (Nove's feasible socialism) but adherents also appeal to principle.

direct-action.rationale: Models rely on elections, reforms and cooperatives; direct action over parliaments is not endorsed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Cooperative experiments (Rochdale, Warren) embody prefiguration, but this is not a stated principle of the mainstream.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; clearly foreign to a model of a modern market economy.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Markets, firms and specialised management remain in all models, so the division of labour is not abolished.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution follows market incomes and profit shares, with only a social dividend for equality, not the need principle of full communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Firms still produce for sale in competitive markets and profits are shared, so production is not organised around use alone.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Some market socialists (Wolff, Roemer) adopt Marxist exploitation theory, others hold that capital ownership skews markets without calling profit exploitation; the field is split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Market socialists present democratic alternatives to dictatorial planning, so reject class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; the models stress cooperatives and worker control but not mandatory collective farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Schweickart blames capitalism for many structural ills but the inevitable-imperialism thesis is not part of the models.

taxation-theft.rationale: The models rely on the capital assets tax and taxation to fund a social dividend, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill's liberal framework includes it, and modern adherents are broadly liberal, but the economic models do not address it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; collective ownership and group rights in firms suggest no rigid individualism.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal democratic left orientation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The models stress democratic voice in firms and public life over exit as the main check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is viewed as a democratic instrument of public investment, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Models are justified by real freedom through democracy at work and equal access to capital and jobs; Schweickart's employer-of-last-resort fits material means to act.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian universalism.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; models use democratic voting and elected legislatures.

total-state.rationale: Opposed by the central idea of decentralised markets and worker self-management.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the models.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the democratic egalitarian orientation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to democratic firm governance.

bound-labor.rationale: Mill and the models aim to end dependent labour and give workers control over their work.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the economics-minded, empirical orientation of the models.

single-common-good.rationale: Models rely on markets and democratic bargaining among interests rather than a single reasoned common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker self-management is the core of Mill's associations, the Yugoslav model, Wolff and Schweickart: one worker, one vote on running firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred preference for public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Schweickart argues that wage deficiency can cause demand shortfalls and favours public investment; inferred opposition to austerity.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mill and market socialists value markets but do not hold that political freedom requires private ownership; the opposite thesis that economic democracy is needed is argued instead.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; models rely on laws and institutions.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the internationalist left orientation.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian orientation suggests universalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Schweickart's public employer of last resort links work and income, but conditioning welfare on work is not stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Worker-run firms remove the employer-worker split by making workers residual claimants; Mill hoped for profit-sharing, but class cooperation as a creed is not stated.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the models.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalist egalitarian orientation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian orientation, and Mill wrote against such legal roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Schweickart's public banks charge no interest on grants through a capital tax that acts as an interest rate, and Proudhon opposed rent and interest, but most models keep an effective cost of capital, so adherents lean against a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian universalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Market socialists see the state as a democratic instrument of investment, not purely a class tool; Marxian strands (Wolff) partly differ.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Schweickart notes environmental harm from capitalism; inferred opposition to expansion.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian liberal orientation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; conspiracy claim is foreign to the models.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the democratic orientation.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the models.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the progressive-left orientation of contemporary adherents.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on populist framing.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal egalitarian orientation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic left orientation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The models require a state for public investment, taxation and market rules.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian universalism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal votes in firms and Mill's equality of terms in associations rest on equal standing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Models such as Yugoslavia's and Schweickart's national designs presume socialism can exist in one country.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal orientation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; no relation to the models.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular left-liberal orientation.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The models aim at democratic markets, not a strengthened state under siege.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not directly stated, but democratic control of firms and public investment rests on consent; Mill is a liberal.

trade-surplus.rationale: Schweickart favours fair trade but no export-surplus goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian liberal orientation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression is not endorsed, since the models rely on taxation and public ownership.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mill defends competition as preventing worse evils and markets reward efficiency, but struggle between peoples as an engine is rejected, so split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Wage workers' dependence on employers is seen as a form of domination; Mill and Schweickart aim to end hired dependence by workers controlling firms.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal democratic orientation.

vanguard-party.rationale: The models rely on democratic firms and elected governments, not a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Schweickart lists poverty among capitalism's structural flaws and favours employment; priority to the poor is inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the pro-labour orientation.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Schweickart attributes poverty to capitalism's structure, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian orientation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic liberal orientation.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Schweickart allows price controls or supports where needed, but most models rely on market prices, so split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic orientation and opposition to party-state systems.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to democratic models.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian orientation.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic orientation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Schweickart favours domestic capital reinvestment and fair trade; no stated view on supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic parliamentary orientation.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular democratic orientation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to democratic orientation.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; reformist adherents unlikely to endorse revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed by the models; Mill's liberalism opposes it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic orientation.

recall-officials.rationale: Mill's workers elect and can remove managers, suggesting the same principle for officials; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Schweickart has firms rent capital from society, so renting is not abolished in principle; housing not addressed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; no relation to the models.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from progressive-left orientation.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-liberal orientation.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from progressive-left orientation.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular orientation.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian orientation.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from progressive orientation.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill championed eccentricity in On Liberty; modern adherents are liberal-left; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Market socialists keep markets and contracts, and the sources do not address sovereign debt; adherents would be split between relief and renegotiation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The model concerns how firms and investment are owned within a country and says nothing on independence; adherents split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The model is an economic design compatible with any constitutional route, so the issue is outside it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Market socialists tie social ownership to democratic worker control, so trading political freedom for growth contradicts it; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Egalitarian aims suggest a duty to the global poor, though aid is not part of the model; Schweickart's model includes fair trade. Inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The economic model is silent, but the democratic egalitarian leanings of adherents point against national nuclear arsenals; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The model says nothing on the head of state and adherents are split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Schweickart's economic democracy has public banks and a capital assets tax directing investment under democratic control, and Lange's board sets capital allocation, which are incompatible with an independent price-stability bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not part of the model; egalitarian, internationalist leanings suggest territory is negotiable for peace; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Market socialists justify ownership by social benefit, putting firms under worker or public control, though their markets keep strong property rights within firms.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Market socialists criticize central planning and Soviet-type economies, but whether to call them state capitalist or flawed socialist varies among adherents.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not a defining issue for an economic model, but its democratic and egalitarian outlook, and Schweickart-style regulation of investment, fit protective environmental action; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Market socialist models are democratic and internationalist-leaning and say little on alliances; inferred that most accept mutual defence among democracies.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from its democratic principles: peoples should decide their own status, so imposed annexation is illegitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Its democratic, liberal-leaning design favours religious freedom and the separation of church and state, not state control of religious bodies; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Modelled mostly on democratic republics and parliaments with ceremonial heads of state; inferred, not a defining issue.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Its democratic principles favour consent of the governed, though the model says nothing directly; Yugoslav self-management ended in secession wars, which adherents treat as a warning, not a doctrine.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Yugoslav-style federalism and economic democracy allow differing local arrangements; inferred as compatible with the model.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The model rests on democratic ownership and control, so a sacred hereditary ruler is incompatible; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Its egalitarian goals and designs such as Roemer coupon schemes or Schweickart capital-asset charges favour progressive rather than flat levies; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Egalitarian reform assumes circumstances shape outcomes; inferred from the belief that changing ownership and opportunity changes lives.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The model is built on democratic self-government and rule of law; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: No stance in the literature and no obvious lean from its principles; adherents are split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Its design favours democratic, one-person-one-vote control of enterprises and politics over rule by an elite; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship conflicts with democratic economic control; inferred from its democratic principles.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian leanings point toward equal parenting but adherents are not clearly united.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Economic democracy aims to end class ownership through worker self-management in a market, with little emphasis on continuing class struggle; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mill's cooperative vision allowed land reform; adherents would likely back redistribution to those who work it; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Egalitarian and democratic leanings support return of refugees; inferred, not discussed in sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nothing in the model supports territorial claims by nationality; inferred from its democratic, internationalist leanings.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Mill's liberal defence of liberty implies opposing legal punishment of religious choice; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal and egalitarian leanings oppose coercing women's dress; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Economic model silent on monetary union; Schweickart-style designs favour regulated trade, so split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not part of the models; inferred from their democratic, civic orientation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the economic models, so split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from democratic and egalitarian leanings; not discussed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The models are about institutions, and the sources do not take a side on historical causation; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Markets are meant to remain competitive and public banks curb concentration; inferred that adherents would back antitrust.

no-bailouts.rationale: Public banks direct investment, but bailout policy is not addressed; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Economic democracy is democratic and constitutional, with courts upheld; inferred, minority rights are valued.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Egalitarian but the economic models do not address representation rules; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Schweickart's model favours regulated fair trade with markets, not an autarkic closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Economic democracy calls for fair trade, with labor and environmental standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Market socialism keeps market prices and incentive signals, so it does not replace material incentives with moral ones.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The models are democratic and institutional, with no role for vanguard action; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mill's egalitarian vision opposed unearned inherited privilege; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Indifferent: an economic model with no stated position on history curricula; nothing in its democratic, egalitarian leanings favours either framing.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, egalitarian principles and self-management ideal, which sit badly with rule over other peoples, though Mill himself defended tutelage of "backward" societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Indifferent: the model concerns ownership of firms; adherents are split on patriotic schooling and the model does not address it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: egalitarian adherents lean toward class-based rather than race-based preferences, but this is contested and not addressed by the model.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the public banks and publicly controlled investment in designs such as Schweickart's economic democracy; public money creation itself is not a defining plank.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Market socialists argue against capitalism on grounds of efficiency, democracy and fairness rather than inevitable collapse, so most accept it can adapt; inferred from how the models are argued.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from democratic and anti-hegemonic leanings; the model does not address imperial legacies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Schweickart's model calls for fair trade and managed capital flows, not a break with the world market, and Yugoslav market socialism traded abroad; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The models target exploitation by capital owners within each economy and assume shared worker interests; inferred as the world-systems claim is not part of them.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian and democratic aims of social ownership, which favour anti-discrimination law over unrestricted owner discretion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, rights-respecting character of the models (economic democracy within a democratic constitution); not directly addressed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Self-determination and democratic consent imply imposed treaties lack legitimacy; inferred, as the model is purely economic.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic control of the economy goes with democratic selection of those who govern; inferred from the model's democratic commitments.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic firms and governments decide by majority vote; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Democratic ideals support removing rulers who break the law; inferred, since the model does not address it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Social ownership is meant to be democratically decided, so elected legislatures over monarchs; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by an economic model; mainstream egalitarian ethics lead adherents to agree; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Mainstream view accepts regulated humane use; inferred, as the model is silent.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aims to remove the large inequalities that make such duties necessary, though a duty to help others is not rejected; adherents split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Democratic firms and economic democracy assume citizens take part; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: An economic model with no settled stance on culture; adherents split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed by the model and adherents differ on how much power rests on consent; split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Market socialists accept world markets and disagree on whether they are exploitative; split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Democratic equality favours open citizenship, but the model is silent; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Yugoslav self-management grew from a split with Moscow, so adherents favour independent national roads; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Models allow foreign trade and capital, and the sources do not address aid; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Favours peaceful settlement of disputes, but the model is silent; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal democratic rights for all citizens oppose leadership by descent; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Democratic socialists oppose fascism and would write that into a constitution; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Condemns both dictatorships, but many resist calling them equivalent; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Consensus history says slavery was the central cause, and an egalitarian view agrees; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Egalitarian leanings favour removal or contextualising over preservation, but the model is silent; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Egalitarian concern with disadvantage leads most adherents to agree; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection and services follow from egalitarian principles, but the model is silent; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Models stress that institutions should suit local conditions, but adherents are divided on civilizational claims; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Democratic control of society conflicts with a political role for the army; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Social provision and egalitarian goals support recognising care as labour; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: The model is economic and says nothing on family duty; adherents are split by culture. Inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Models stress democratic control, with elected managers in firms and public boards accountable to citizens, over examination-selected rulers; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Public control of capital and fair-trade rules in models such as Schweickart's support limits on foreign takeovers; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Egalitarian and liberal-democratic leanings favour easy divorce; inferred, not a topic of the model.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mill and later models have managers elected by workers and removable by them; extended to political representatives by inference.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social ownership of capital and a citizens' dividend, not private investment accounts, are the models' answer on retirement income; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Social ownership extends to natural resources and capital in most models, with Mill favouring taxing land rents; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The models are democratic and assume legislative control of public funds; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Yugoslav self-management and liberal-egalitarian leanings favoured multilingual equality; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: No model addresses it, but liberal-egalitarian leanings and trade integration favour equal treatment; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Egalitarian aims lead most adherents to look at outcomes as well as intent; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Egalitarian and anti-wage-labour views make adherents critical of consumer culture, though the model keeps consumer markets; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Democratic, egalitarian leanings and no foreign-policy doctrine suggest opposing covert proxy wars; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Yugoslavia's self-management model arose by defying Soviet bloc control, and self-determination is assumed; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic democracy treats concentrated private capital as a threat to democratic government; inferred, not stated.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are inferred to be split between sovereignty and civil-society concerns.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an egalitarian, internationalist-leaning economic model.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; the models are about firms and capital, and would not favour residency barriers.

job-guarantee.rationale: Schweickart's economic democracy proposes full-employment policies and public investment; the job guarantee itself is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the model is economic and adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; inferred to be split, since the model relies on a democratic state and rule of law but is not about political obligation.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are inferred to be split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Self-managed firms in a market economy organise by enterprise, so industrial versus craft unions is not central; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its democratic egalitarian orientation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred to be split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic accountability of firms and public investment banks.

local-production.rationale: Markets allow trade at any distance and sources do not address localism; inferred to be split.

informal-organisation.rationale: The models depend on formal firms, banks and elected institutions, not informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a democratic egalitarian internationalist orientation.

religious-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular democratic orientation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Market socialism has no view on tribute among states; its egalitarian and democratic leanings suggest equal dealings; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Egalitarian aims suggest pooling across regions, though some designs favour local enterprise ownership; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Social ownership applies to firms and capital, while personal property remains; inferred from the models.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not a defining issue; adherents favour peaceful coexistence with other economic systems; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Competitive markets with public funding and cooperative or public firms fit the models; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not a defining issue for an economic model, and Marxist and non-Marxist adherents differ; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mill and Marxist-influenced strands see capitalism as having developed production; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Egalitarian leanings suggest support, though the model does not address it; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The model is about markets and enterprise ownership and does not require socialised housework; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a defining issue; liberal and democratic leanings favour a living language; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Democratic, egalitarian leanings favour keeping lasting promises; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Models keep nation-states and markets with cooperatives as firms, not communal society; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not a defining issue; democratic leanings oppose steering settlement; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The models reject both capitalist ownership and comprehensive central planning, a third course between them.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: market socialism is an economic model with an egalitarian, universalist outlook that gives no weight to ancestral land claims over current residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, egalitarian commitments; no strand of the model denies documented atrocities.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the model's democratic and liberal-leaning adherents treat private adult conduct as outside the law; the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Market socialism rests on democratic enterprise control and political pluralism, so suppressing opposition contradicts it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, secular-neutral framework; the sources do not discuss blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: social ownership and economic democracy are incompatible with governing territories for a ruling country's profit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the model has no religious-law doctrine, and its adherents would not frame armed resistance as a religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: authority rests on democratic consent in these models, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Worker self-management and economic democracy put decisions in the hands of those affected, in firms and communities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian leanings; the economic model does not address intersectionality directly.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian and liberal-democratic leanings; the sources do not discuss it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Adherents are split on this and the economic model is silent on it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: market socialism sees itself as a left project that combines markets with social ownership, not as a post-left synthesis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Market socialism aims to end wage labour by making workers co-owners and self-directing, answering the alienation critique.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, egalitarian outlook; the sources do not discuss it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from its democratic principle that firms and the state answer to their members and citizens; Mill's text is secular in argument.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are split and the economic model is silent on it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its pro-worker leanings and its emphasis on employee rights; not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Market socialism accepts markets and welfare but rejects capitalist ownership, so adherents would only partly endorse a capitalist-style social market.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: no market-socialist source calls for abolishing armed forces; its egalitarian leanings give some sympathy to disarmament.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the model aims at equality through social ownership or citizen dividends, not allowing some to prosper first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Foreign policy is outside the economic model and adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The model rests on democratic, worker-elected control of firms and public bodies; inherited supreme office conflicts with that, though the sources do not discuss it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist ancestors favoured user-owned credit, but modern designs such as Schweickart's use publicly run investment banks, so adherents are split; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian aim of curbing inequality, which sits badly with externally imposed spending cuts; the sources never address IMF conditionality.

property-franchise.rationale: A model built on ending wealth-based control of firms would not tie votes to wealth; inferred from its democratic principles.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The model is an economic design that is silent on ecofeminism; adherents range from Marxist-feminist to indifferent, so no direction is inferred.

reification.rationale: Marxist-influenced market socialists such as Wolff may accept the critique, but the family's core claim is that markets are a useful coordinating device, so adherents are split.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Concern that wealth concentration distorts democracy runs through the egalitarian case for social ownership; inferred, not stated on the press specifically.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Competitive markets and elected enterprise management presuppose predictable, published rules; inferred rather than stated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Democratic, egalitarian ownership rules the family out of restricting political rights by race; inferred from its principles.

online-participation.rationale: Economic democracy stresses broad participation in decisions, which adherents would likely extend to online tools; anachronistic inference.

open-government-data.rationale: Public investment banks and public enterprises under democratic control imply public accountability and openness; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Nothing in the model supports legal limits on marriage, and its liberal-egalitarian outlook opposes them; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting shops by owners' religion contradicts the egalitarian, cooperative ethos; inferred from principles.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not a topic of the model, but its core idea is democratic control, by workers over firms and citizens over investment; lot-chosen deliberative bodies fit that participatory spirit. Inferred from the economic-democracy emphasis, not from a stated position.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed by market socialism; as an economic model its adherents lean secular-progressive and favour modernising readings of religion. Inferred from those general leanings.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Market socialism exists to end the concentration of capital in private hands; Schweickart-style economic democracy and Roemer's coupon design aim to stop wealth translating into power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the egalitarian, democratic leanings of the model's modern proponents, who mostly sit on the progressive left.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: modern market socialists favour democratic, pluralist institutions and enterprise self-management, which sits badly with state-imposed belief, though Yugoslav-era regimes were hostile to religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the model concerns firm ownership and markets, not policing; its proponents work within democratic states that keep ordinary public safety institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The model is silent on constitutional design for divided societies, and its adherents have no common position on consociationalism versus majority rule.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Market socialists seek a more equal economy through institutional design and public provision, not reliance on voluntary charity, which they see as inadequate to structural inequality.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents are indifferent or split between term limits and the democratic preference for letting voters choose.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in market socialist literature; its stress on democratic participation is compatible with it but does not require it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: not a theme of the literature, but a democratic egalitarian left generally accepts that avoiding extinction is a public priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the gender-egalitarian and democratic leanings of modern proponents; the model itself says nothing about religious institutions.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the model's egalitarian and democratic ethos applied to the household; not addressed directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Economic democracy extends democratic participation to all who work and live in a community, so resident voting fits; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Market socialists accept price signals and are split over capping rents in a shortage versus expanding supply; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Market socialists keep competitive markets and incentives, which many defend with intellectual property; inferred from the model.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed; the democratic, egalitarian leanings of the model are the opposite of drilled national youth movements; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the model; democratic socialist leanings suggest support for removing nuclear weapons; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents lean towards opposing foreign bases from egalitarian, anti-militarist leanings; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the model; democratic leanings suggest support for official recognition of past atrocities; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Schweickart's capital assets tax and worker self-management aim to end income from mere ownership while keeping pay for work, though markets still reward investment through returns to firms.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed by the model; most adherents would accept lethal force as a last resort; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; the model's democratic, egalitarian leanings do not support myths of ancient continuity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; an economic model without a position, adherents are split; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; an economic model without a position, adherents are split; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; democratic, egalitarian leanings reject sacralising the national dead; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not addressed; the model treats politics as institutions and economic design, not cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents are split; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents are split; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents are indifferent; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian leanings favour judging traditions by the full humanity of women; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not addressed; the model's egalitarian and open-market principles reject reserving economic roles for a national majority; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed by the model; adherents are split; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Worker-run firms with democratic management imply unions that answer to members; the sources do not discuss union independence, so this is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Self-management by workers is the defining feature of the main models, so workers' real power is what makes them socialist, but Lange's version gives the state a large role.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Schweickart's model keeps basic services public alongside market enterprises; inferred for local services.

second-chamber.rationale: The economic models take no position on legislative structure; inferred indifference.

municipal-property.rationale: In Mill's and Schweickart's models the firm is controlled by its own workers and capital is held by society, not owned by the municipality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The models coordinate through markets and a central investment mechanism, not confederations of assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Market socialism pays by contribution or enterprise income through markets, though some models add a social dividend; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The economic models take no position on drug regulation; inferred indifference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The economic models take no position on ageing research; inferred indifference.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The models run on market exchange and public banks and take no position on payment privacy; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: The economic models do not address online identity; inferred indifference.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's liberal individualism and the democratic emphasis of the modern models favour the person against the state; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The economic models take no position on human spirituality; inferred indifference.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The models take no position on territorial government; inferred indifference.

gm-crops.rationale: The economic models take no position on genetic engineering; inferred indifference.

dense-cities.rationale: The economic models take no position on urban form; inferred indifference.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The egalitarian, class-based outlook of the models leans against organising politics by race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: The universalist, egalitarian leanings of the tradition lean against racial pride; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The democratic and egalitarian leanings of the modern models lean toward defensive force only; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: An economic model with no doctrine of nationhood; adherents are split, so it is left neutral, inferred from the model's silence on the question.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the model's democratic, egalitarian leanings, which favour common electorates over religiously separate ones.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not part of the model; inferred that its internationally minded academic adherents would treat such claims as exaggerated.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from the egalitarian aim of widening opportunity through public provision of basics (Schweickart's economic democracy includes free public services).

pollution-taxes.rationale: Market socialists rely on prices and markets, and Schweickart's model uses taxes on capital assets; a polluter-pays tax fits that market logic, inferred rather than stated.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the general egalitarian and ecological concern of modern market socialists such as Schweickart.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the model's universalist, class-based egalitarianism does not single out gendered values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not discussed by the model; inferred from the left-egalitarian leanings of its adherents.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the model's democratic accountability emphasis, not stated in sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Public control of investment is central, but this concerns domestic allocation; adherents are split on cross-border limits.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not a concern of the model; adherents who accept a democratic state would accept its monopoly of force. Inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream adherents work through democratic states and do not urge disobedience in the army. Inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Where firms are not worker-owned, social ownership aims at fairer pay; unions and bargaining are generally supported, though worker self-management reduces the need.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Adherents prefer changing ownership to top-ups, but many accept them as redistribution; inferred and split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Economic democracy designs rely on public investment decided democratically, which binding borrowing limits would constrain; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Egalitarian leanings suggest sympathy, but it is not part of the model; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Market socialism works through democratic institutions and public enterprises, not revolutionary destruction of the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The models are specific blueprints, yet they are explicitly experimental and plural; adherents are split. Inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Pricing resources in markets suits the model, but social ownership aims to put ecology above profit; inferred and split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian and democratic leanings make sacralising the nation unlikely. Inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Egalitarian goals suggest support for relieving debt; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed by the model; inferred as indifferent.

shared-human-nature.rationale: An economic model with no stated view on human nature; inferred as neutral.

public-service-media.rationale: Public provision of basic goods suggests support for independent public media; inferred from the egalitarian goals.

religions-one-truth.rationale: An economic model with no stated view on religion; adherents are typically secular and pluralist, so this is a weak inference.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cooperative credit and public support for farmers fit a model that wants social ownership and public banking, though price floors distort markets; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The model is silent on defence and adherents split between pacifist and mainstream-left positions; neutral inference.

workers-own-party.rationale: Adherents are split between working-class parties and broad social-democratic parties; the model itself is silent.

ban-fgm.rationale: Egalitarian and rights-based liberal commitments lead most adherents to support a ban; inferred, as the model is economic.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property and inheritance rights follow from the model's egalitarian aims; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The model has no view on how languages are classified; neutral inference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Market socialists accept regulating externalities through public rules and taxes rather than leaving them to lawsuits, as in Schweickart's capital charges; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Democratic, egalitarian principles favour elected bodies over hereditary or customary advisers; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Market socialists accept regulation of externalities but hold liberal views on individual freedom, and the question is outside the model; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Egalitarian reformers generally prefer judicial discretion and rehabilitation to fixed sentences; inferred, outside the model.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The model is silent on immigration and language, and adherents are split; neutral inference.

missingStatements.text: Banks and the funds for new investment should be publicly controlled so that society, not private savers, decides where capital goes.
missingStatements.rationale: Schweickart's model uses a capital assets tax and public banks to direct investment without interest, and Lange's board sets capital allocation.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should receive a regular dividend from publicly owned capital.
missingStatements.rationale: Roemer's coupon economy, Bardhan and Corneo's proposals distribute capital income to all citizens as a social dividend.

notes: Strands differ on public versus cooperative ownership and on how far planning should simulate markets. Marxist-influenced writers such as Wolff accept exploitation theory while others do not. Only the first 100,000 characters of the Wikipedia pages were read.
